text: Hey, and welcome to the MX-5 guide on
Summit Point Raceway in iRacing. If you
want to, then you can practice against
my ghost car. You can find the lap files
on our community Discord, which is
linked in the description down below,
and you can find the telemetry on
Garrett 61.
There's always a lot of action on the
main straight because the first braking
zone is the only spot where you can
overtake. So, always check your
surroundings and defend or attack on the
inside line right here, or stick to the
outside line, which I'm using right now,
if you're going for a fast lap.
Position your car on the left edge of
the track and brake at the halfway point
between the three and two cones. You
want to go hard on the brakes and shift
all the way down into first gear.
You want to stick to the left and turn
in very late, shortly before you reach
this patched-up part of the track. You
can use the manual blip into first gear,
like I'm doing it right now, to get a
smoother run into the first turn, but
it's not mandatory. You can still finish
a good lap time without it.
Aim for a smooth line. Be gentle on the
throttle when you engage it again and
avoid the inside curb, as well as the
inside of the exit in general. You want
to keep some distance to the white line
because shortly after the curb, the
inside will become very rough and bumpy,
and if you drive right over it, it will
hurt your exit.
Approach the next turn on the right edge
of the track and give the brakes a super
soft touch when you approach the end of
the pathway on the right hand side. You
don't want to brake a lot. You want to
slow down just enough to make the turn.
Aim for a smooth line and attack the
throttle. You can also take the curb a
bit, but don't be too aggressive over it
because then it will push you to the
right and enter the gravel, so stay a
bit cautious.
If you touch the gravel, then it's no
big deal. You won't receive an incident
point as long as the center of your car
stays above the curb. Just make sure
that you don't lift because you don't
want to lose any speed around here.
Around here you want to align the car
with the left edge of the track and
stick to it for as long as you can.
I don't have a good turn and marker for
this turn, but after a few laps you will
develop a good feeling for it. As you
can see, I'm still driving on the left
edge of the track because you want to
turn in as late as possible because that
way you don't need to lift for the next
apex.
Straighten the wheel as soon as you make
the turn and go hard on the brakes. You
want to shift all the way down into
first gear and let the car swing to the
right edge of the track.
You can use a manual blip on your
downshift into first gear again to get a
bit more control over the car. From that
point on you want to aim for a smooth
line and attack the inside curb on the
exit. Stay in first gear and keep
pushing the car to the left.
Push the car all the way to the left
edge of the track and give the brakes a
soft touch when you reach this barrier
to get a smooth line around the next
right-hander.
There aren't any specific tricks for the
next section. All you want to keep in
mind is that you want to stay on the
throttle and hit smooth lines around the
next three turns.
There's some dirt on the outside of the
last turn which you want to use as
marker and hit the brakes when you reach
it. You want to push them down with
roughly 25% pressure, shift down into
third gear, and point the car towards
the next apex.
In the last turn there are two important
things to keep in mind. Number one is
that you want to attack the throttle as
early as possible because we're heading
onto a long straight, so any speed you
lose around here will cost you a lot all
the way down to the next braking zone.
And number two is that you avoid the
inside curb because touching it would
unsettle your car. So, make sure that
you hit the clean line right around it.
